clue.text: Sudden cold weather to continue slowly? That’ll do for flower

blocks.note: a cold snap is a sudden spell of cold weather
to drag on is to continue tediously

explanation.surface: A gardener wonders which bloom can survive a cold snap followed by a long, dragging winter.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark after the weather half hints that the phrase is to be read as two separate chunks, SNAP and DRAG ON.

clue.text: Player who hasn’t practised, one sounding resigned about pace

clue.text: Risk missing first walk

clue.text: Affair to get aggravated, having many people crammed in van

clue.text: Strauss heroine’s solo with soaring finale

clue.text: Completely finished with FBI man given too much to take in?

definitions.text: given too much to take in

blocks.note: a fed is a US federal agent

clue.text: Easily distracted person dropping bishop in country

clue.text: A rich colour’s dispersed, with no large arrangement of shades

clue.text: Sense of occasion, raising it with former Chinese leadership

clue.text: Old Italian and French sport overview

clue.text: Revised reading incorporating live material

clue.text: Poet, foremost of ones in English Literature

clue.text: A period with female expert producing change of opinion

clue.text: Way information will restrict old source of disease

clue.text: Rural workers last to attend soccer club?

clue.text: Bandage son with two articles
